purpose: Isolate C/Zig i386 by-value aggregate interoperability from Herdr and the iSH emulator.
probe_safety: Output pointer is first; both languages declare the same initialized trailing u32 argument. No wrong-prototype aliases, variadic calls, or uninitialized output contents are used.

linux_docker_i386_execution.execution_note: Existing binfmt executes the i386 ELF; no registration or global Docker changes. This is not native i386 hardware.

assembly_observation.interpretation: Zig separates adjacent u16 fields into individual i386 argument words although C packs them into a single word; extern struct memory layout agrees but by-value calling convention does not.

build_commands: zig build-obj experiments/zig-i386-abi/echo.zig -target x86-linux-musl -mcpu pentium -O ReleaseSmall -femit-bin=OUT/echo.o -femit-asm=OUT/echo.s
zig cc -target x86-linux-musl -mcpu=pentium -static -O1 -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror experiments/zig-i386-abi/probe.c OUT/reference.o OUT/echo.o -o OUT/probe
conclusion: The by-value mismatch is independently present without Herdr and reproduces outside iSH. Pointer-based C/Zig interoperation passes these cases. A correctly typed C ABI wrapper is a possible repair to investigate; no Herdr/library repair is implemented by this probe.
